x: At the start Belgrave were well to the fore, Duffett taking the lead, followed by Footer, Pyer and Tame. Soon after came Khlopin, Smith, Rice and Pritchard These positions were maintained practically throughout the race, and excellent packing enabled us to win quite comfortably
…ayliss headed the field on the short lap, but was quickly displaced by Clark and Tibbutt with Duffett, Rice, Footer and Pyer just behind.…
Pyer was then in the first 15 followed by Rice and Bayliss a dozen yards away. Coming back from the country, Pyer was still leading our men with Smith and Footer 30 or 40 yards away.
After the start the field soon spread out, and at the first mile Clark led Duffett by a yard or two, with Pyer, Webb, Footer and Khlopin about 40 yards behind, and the rest following in close order.

Pyer was next home for us filling 56th position. The remaining two places in the scoring team were filled by W Mitchell, 125th (who was running in his first big race for the club), and A Clark, 133rd, who finished just in front of W.
Our first man, Micky Pyer, was left in readiness at Westminster, and the 'bus started off at 10.45 a.m. for the first change-over at Nightingale Lane.
Team Race—Belgrave H , 1 , Rice, 1 ; Pyer, 2 , Bayliss, 4 , Flower, 6 Mitcham A C , 2, 3-5-6, 7pts ; Croydon H., 3, 7-10-11, 14 pts. , Epsom H , 4, 8-9-12, 29 pts Time 4m. 44 4-5s.

Khlopin, as we expected was leading round the rather dangerous bend some hundred yards from the start, but he was soon passed by Cohen and Pyer.

George's, and Tebbutt of S.L.H., who was representing the London Scottish, well in the lead, followed by Pyer and Bayliss. After 2 miles had been covered Duffett joined the leaders, while Bayliss had dropped a few places.
It will be seen that we had four men in eight at this point, with Rice and Footer running 18th, and 19th; and, as Smith and Pyer were within striking distance, our chances appeared very rosy.
Pyer was the "star," with a dogged little chap named Footer always after his body. Well, one day Footer beat Pyer, and I cannot recall him playing second fiddle since!

Then came the Bels- Pyer, Penny, Duffett, Bill Webb and so on, and we won with 77pts, to the 275 of Ashcombe and 276 of TVH. A fortnight later the event moved to Wimbledon where there were over 100 starters, 60 of them Belgravians.
